newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO steady to firm on Chinese demand.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO steady to firm on Chinese demand.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices were assessed steady to firm as Chinese buying ahead of the festive season in early February is expected to prop up prices, traders said on Monday.
Chinese inventories are currently at very low levels and aggressive buyers emerged to replenish stocks before the festive season starts, a trader told Reuters.
Taiwan floated a tender to buy up to 78,000 tonnes of low sulphur fuel oil for delivery in January. The tender closes December 18 and is valid until December 20.
Traders said fundamentals were tight with limited South Korean supplies as refiners run more sweet crudes to produce more distillates for the winter.
But the Singapore cargo market was lacklustre on Monday with no bids or offers heard. High sulphur 180-cst grade fuel oil was quoted at $121-$123 per tonne on Friday.
In the swaps market, December was down at $120/$120.50, a dollar lower from Friday's quotes.
